annotatedSteps.description: Definition of variables and expressions for time
annotatedSteps.studentWork:
Let the speed of the train be x km/h. Reduced speed = (x − 8) km/h.
Time at usual speed = 480/x, time at reduced speed = 480/(x − 8).
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correct definition of variables and time expressions

annotatedSteps.description: Forming the equation according to given condition
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: × Incorrect order of subtraction; lower speed takes longer time, so 480/(x − 8) − 480/x = 3

annotatedSteps.description: Simplifying the formed equation into standard quadratic form
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correct algebraic simplification of student's own equation (ECF applied)

annotatedSteps.description: Rejection of negative root and final statement with units
annotatedSteps.studentWork:
Speed cannot be negative.
∴ Speed of the train = 40 km/h.
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correct context-based root rejection and final conclusion with units

teacherNote: Remember that time taken at a reduced speed is greater than time at usual speed, so the larger fraction 480/(x − 8) must come first. Be careful with signs during factorization, as (x − 40)(x + 32) corresponds to a constant term of −1280 rather than +1280.

rubric.point: Defining speed variables and expressing time taken for both speeds
Setting up the correct time difference equation: 480/(x − 8) − 480/x = 3
Simplifying the algebraic equation to standard quadratic form
Solving the quadratic equation to find the roots
Rejecting negative root with reason and stating final speed with units
